battle.name: 劉元進起義
battle.theater: 徽州歙縣與新安江下游
battle.brief: 大業九年冬，歙縣人劉元進在徽州舉兵，自稱太守，攻陷歙、黟一帶縣邑，與同年吳郡劉子元之亂相應。隋廷主力壓在高句麗前線，江淮空虛，屢遣官軍討之，戰事延至隋亡。起義者多持竹木槊與柴刀改造的長刀，官軍則以環首刀、陌刀、槊與蹶張弩為骨幹；卡面的月牙劍正是這類單刃彎刀的祖型。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 大業九年爆發的這場叛亂，交戰一方是隋朝官軍，另一方是劉元進為首的江淮起義軍。隋朝方面：全國兵制以十二衛與各軍府為骨幹，府兵在文帝時尚能按期番上，到煬帝時因連年征高句麗、興造江都與洛陽的宮室、漕轉而崩壞，兵源改以募兵為主，郡縣的團兵、鄉兵也被推上前線；鎮壓起義多由行軍總管、驍騎將軍、虎賁郎將率領臨時編成的討平軍，後方靠江都、丹陽的宿衛與自江北抽調的援軍支應，糧秣則沿運河自江南運往。起義軍方面：劉元進是歙縣人，起事後自稱太守，靠歙、黟一帶的流民、逃戶、散兵與亡命之徒聚眾，器械多取自民間，竹木桿槊、弓弩、柴刀與農具改造的長刀並用，也有從郡縣武庫中奪得的少量甲兵與環首刀；他們沒有固定編制與後方，糧食靠掠取與新安江的水運，戰術以流動游擊、避城攻堅、襲擊郡縣治所為主。放在當時的大局裏，這場叛亂是隋朝全面崩解的一角：高句麗前線吸走了最後一批精兵與國力，江淮因徭役與饑荒而空虛，河北的竇建德、山東的王薄等起義又分散了平叛的力量，劉元進能在徽州站住腳，正是因為隋廷在江南的手已經伸不直。
countriesEn: The revolt that broke out in the ninth year of the Daye era was fought between the armies of the Sui government on one side and the Jianghuai insurgents led by Liu Yuanjin on the other. On the Sui side the military order rested on the twelve imperial guards and the army prefectures scattered around the empire. The fubing levies still rendered their periodic service under Emperor Wen, but under Yangdi they had fallen apart: repeated campaigns against Goguryeo, the building of the palaces at Jiangdu and Luoyang, and the endless hauling of grain had worn the system out, so that troops hired by payment replaced it as the main source of manpower, while county militia and village levies were pushed into the line as well. Punitive expeditions were usually led by a xingjun zongguan, a cavalry general or a commander of the Tiger Guards, heading a force patched together for the occasion, supported from the rear by the garrisons of Jiangdu and Danyang and by units recalled from north of the Yangtze, with grain and provisions moved up through the canal. On the insurgents' side, Liu Yuanjin was a native of She County; after raising his revolt he proclaimed himself governor, gathering followers among the displaced people, the absentees from the tax registers, disbanded soldiers and desperate men around She and Yi. Their weapons came mostly out of civilian life: bamboo and wooden lances, bows and crossbows, sickles and long knives reworked from farm tools, with a few suits of armour and ring-pommel sabres taken from county armouries. They had no regular establishment and no rear area; they lived on plunder and on the water of the Xin'an River, and their method was to move about, to refuse to hold cities for long, and to strike at the seats of county and prefectural government. Set in the wider picture, this revolt was one corner of a general Sui collapse. The Goguryeo front had drawn off the last of the trained soldiers and of the state's resources; the Jianghuai had been hollowed out by corvée and famine; and revolts such as Dou Jiande's in the north and Wang Bo's in Shandong divided the forces available for suppression. That Liu Yuanjin could hold his ground in Huizhou was precisely because the Sui court's hand no longer reached into Jiangnan.
people: 劉元進是歙縣人，籍貫就在這場叛亂的中心地帶。史籍關於他早年的記載極少，只知他原是地方上的小吏或鄉里豪右，能號召鄉民；大業九年冬他在歙州起兵，自稱太守（另有一說稱王），攻下歙、黟等縣，聲勢延伸到宣州、饒州一帶。隋廷視他為江淮心腹之患，遣軍討之，數度將他打散，他卻屢次復起，至大業十三年仍據徽州活動。同一時期江南還有數場與他並起的叛亂：吳郡的劉子元在該年自稱吳王，兵眾一度號稱十餘萬，很快被隋軍平定，姓名與劉元進相近，後世常把兩人相提；舒州的陳佛智、吳郡的沈興國、杭州的汪文進則在大業十三年陸續舉兵，與劉元進遙相呼應。隋朝方面的關鍵人物是煬帝楊廣本人：他一面把主力壓在遼東的高句麗戰線上，一面靠江都、丹陽的宿衛與臨時徵集的募兵去平地方叛亂，兩頭爭的是同一批兵與同一批糧；遼東方向還有奉詔西討楊玄感的武衛大將軍宇文化及，以及在河北自行坐大的竇建德、在山東起兵的義師首領王薄。真正做出關鍵決定的是隋廷自己：每一次是否從江都抽調宿衛、是否暫緩北征、是否改派能打的部隊，決定了徽州山區的攻防能拖多久，也決定了這場叛亂最終是成為改朝換代的力量，還是被壓回山裡。
peopleEn: Liu Yuanjin was a native of She County, so the seat of this rebellion was the country he came from. What the histories record about his earlier life is very little: he was a minor local official or a village notable of some standing, and he could call up country people. In the winter of the ninth year of Daye (613) he raised troops in Shezhou and proclaimed himself governor (one account says king); he took She and Yi and other counties, and his strength reached toward Xuanzhou and Raozhou. The Sui court treated him as the bane of the Jianghuai, sent troops against him, scattered him more than once, and watched him rise again; as late as the thirteenth year of Daye (617) he was still operating in Huizhou. Several other revolts in the south ran alongside his that year. In Wujun, Liu Ziyuan proclaimed himself King of Wu in the same year, his following claimed at one point to run to more than a hundred thousand, and he was put down quickly by Sui troops; his name is close to Liu Yuanjin's, and later writers often pair the two. In Shuzhou, Chen Fozhi; in Wujun, Shen Xingguo; and in Hangzhou, Wang Wenjin raised banners in the thirteenth year of Daye, answering Liu Yuanjin from a distance. The key figure on the Sui side was Yangdi himself. He kept the bulk of his forces committed to the Goguryeo front in Liaodong while relying on the garrisons of Jiangdu and Danyang and on hastily enrolled paid troops to put down local revolts, and the two demands competed for the same men and the same grain. On the Liaodong side stood Wanyan Huaji, commander of the Martial Guards, who was sent west to deal with Yang Xuanggan's rising, along with Dou Jiande, who was building a power of his own in the north, and Wang Bo, who had raised a righteous army in Shandong. The decisive judgements were the court's own: every decision to move the Jiangdu garrison, to suspend the northern expedition, or to substitute troops who could actually fight determined how long the fighting in the mountains of Huizhou would last, and so determined whether this rising would become a force that changed the dynasty or would be pushed back into the hills.
kits: 卡面上這件古埃及月牙劍，與隋軍的兵裝沒有任何直接傳承關係：它是約前一千五百年的形制，單刃、刀身強烈前曲，刃口開在弧線內側，砍進目標後回拉即能切得更深，不必像直刃那樣拔出。隋軍手上的對應物是環首刀與陌刀。環首刀刀身微弧、刃口同樣開在內弧，與月牙劍「砍了不必拔」的刀法邏輯相通，卻是直刃格鬥傳統的形制，隋墓出土的環首刀多配長柲，供步兵佩用；陌刀則是直刃長柄、雙手握持，隋文帝時曾以之賜騎士，主要用來破騎兵、斬馬足，與環首刀分工明確。除此之外，隋軍的裝備還包括兜鍪、札甲與兩當鎧、明光甲等護具，橫刀、長槊與短柄刀，角弓與桑木弓、大量箭矢，蹶張弩與臂弩這類弩機；攻城則備雲梯、撞車、巢車、擲石機與猛火油櫓，穴城掘進亦是常法；騎兵有甲馬與馬鐙，後勤靠大業元年開通的通濟渠與大業四年北抵涿郡的永濟渠轉運，沿線設驛。起義軍的裝備與之相比簡陋得多：竹木桿槊、柴刀、斧、鍬與弓弩為主，甲兵極少，多是破舊皮甲或從郡縣武庫中奪來的零星器物，攻城器械與騎兵基本沒有，跨江靠小船，也靠冬春枯水期涉水。這種裝備差異本身就說明問題：國家軍工供應已告中斷，一場戰爭勝負往往不在戰鬥意志，而在後勤。
kitsEn: The khopesh on the card has no direct line of descent to the equipment of the Sui army. It is a form of about 1500 BC: single-edged, with a blade curved sharply forward and the edge set on the inside of the curve, so that once it bites into a target, drawing it back carries the edge deeper instead of having to pull a straight blade free. The Sui answer to it was the ring-pommel sabre and the miodao. The ring-pommel sabre has a slightly curved blade with the edge likewise on the inner arc, and so shares the cutting logic of the khopesh, that a blow need not be withdrawn; it belongs, however, to the tradition of the straight-edged single blade, and the ring-pommel sabres excavated from Sui tombs are mostly fitted with a long tang and carried by foot soldiers. The miodao is something else again: a straight edge on a long haft, gripped with two hands, and given by Emperor Wen to cavalry, its business being to break cavalry and to cut at horses' legs, a clear division of labour with the sabre. Beyond those, the Sui order of battle included the helmet, lamellar and sleeveless armour and the bright plate of the Ming Guang harness; the hengdao, the long lance and short-hafted blades; the horn and mulberry bows with a large stock of arrows; crossbows of the crushing and the arm type; and for siege, scaling ladders, battering rams, observation towers, stone-throwers and fire-oil carts, with tunnelling into the walls a standard practice as well. The cavalry had armoured horses and stirrups, and the rear services ran on the Tongji Canal opened in the first year of Daye and the Yongji Canal reaching north to Zhuojun in the fourth, with post stations along the line. The insurgents' equipment was much poorer by comparison: bamboo and wooden lances, sickles, axes, hoes, bows and crossbows were the core, armour was very scarce and mostly worn leather or whatever could be taken from county armouries, and they had neither siege engines nor cavalry; they crossed the river in small boats and by wading in the winter and spring when the water was low. The difference in equipment says enough on its own: the state's war industries had already broken down, and the outcome of such a war turned far more often on logistics than on fighting spirit.
tactics: 起義軍的戰術是一套典型的山地游擊辦法。他們選在秋冬江淮水勢平穩、而隋廷主力正陷在遼東的窗口起事，行動以襲擊郡縣治所為主：夜渡新安江、屯聚村塢，趁郡兵尚未集結便攻歙、黟；被追擊時散入徽州山嶺與鄉里險隘，官軍退走即重新聚合，不與官軍主力正面野戰，也不打算久守城池。攻城靠雲梯、穴城與急攻三種辦法，甲兵不足就用血肉之軀換時間，奪城之後不久又棄。糧食靠掠取與水運維持，戰線因此始終貼著新安江與歙、黟、績溪一帶的鄉村。隋軍這邊的處境正好相反：初派郡兵與募兵討之，既缺乏經驗也缺乏攻城器械與糧食，常一觸即潰，兵潰之後又各自散去為盜；後來才集中驍騎與虎賲宿衛，由江都沿運河北上，以據城固守、待敵疲於奔命、然後出城反擊為主，並配合鄉村鎮撫、斷絕糧道與往來搜查，把叛軍壓在徽州山地和鄰近州縣之內。雙方共同的關鍵變量是兵源與糧秣：隋廷不敢從高句麗前線抽調太多兵員，叛軍也拿不到攻城的重械，於是整場戰事成了一場漫長的拉鋸，直到隋朝自身崩潰才由別的力量收場。
tacticsEn: The insurgents fought in the manner of mountain partisans. They chose the moment when the waters of the Jianghuai were quiet in the autumn and winter, while the bulk of the Sui army was bogged down in Liaodong, and their action consisted above all of raids on the seats of county government: crossing the Xin'an River by night, massing in the farmsteads and hamlets, and striking at She and Yi before the county militia could assemble. When pursued they scattered into the mountains of Huizhou and the defiles of the countryside, and re-formed once the Sui troops withdrew; they avoided set-piece battle against the main body of the government army and had no intention of holding cities for long. In attacking towns they used scaling ladders, tunnelling and a rush, and since armour was scarce they spent lives to buy time, taking a city and then leaving it again before long. Food came from plunder and from the river, so the line of operations stayed close to the Xin'an River and the villages of She, Yi and Jixi. The situation of the Sui army was the exact opposite. At first it was sent county militia and hired troops, which had neither experience nor siege engines nor supplies, and which often broke at the first contact, the broken men then going off in bands to become bandits. Only later did the court concentrate the cavalry and the Tiger Guard garrison, move north from Jiangdu along the canal, and adopt a method of holding strongpoints, waiting for the enemy to tire itself out in running, and then counter-attacking from the walls, combined with pacification in the villages, cutting of the enemy's food and repeated searching, so as to pin the rebels inside the mountains of Huizhou and the neighbouring prefectures and counties. The variable that mattered to both sides was men and grain. The court dared not draw many more troops away from the Goguryeo front, and the rebels could not get the heavy engines for a siege, so the whole war became a long grinding contest, to be finished only when the Sui itself collapsed and other forces closed the matter.
data: 可以核對的數字大致如下。這場起義記在大業九年，即公元六一三年；《隋書·煬帝紀》與《資治通鑑》都只給出年月而無具體日子，一般記在該年十月至十一月之間。劉元進的起兵不是孤例：同年吳郡有劉子元起兵自稱吳王，黎陽有楊玄感舉事，山東一線則有王薄在此前已起兵的義師，河北的竇建德也在隋廷失去控制的地方坐大。隋朝的國力數字同樣見於史載：據《資治通鑑》，大業年間第二次征高句麗，兵逾百萬；運河工程方面，大業元年開通濟渠直抵江都，大業四年開永濟渠北抵涿郡；《隋書·食貨志》記大業中天下戶八百九十餘萬、口四千六百餘萬，每一兵卒背後對應的丁口與轉輸量，都是這場平叛難以承受的規模。起義本身的兵數沒有可靠數字留下，諸史只以「眾數萬」一類的概數記載，劉元進部的確切人數至今無人能定；可以確定的只是他並非小股盜匪，而是一度被隋廷視為江淮最大威脅的勢力之一。時間上，從六一三年冬起兵到六一八年隋亡，前後至少四年多，期間隋廷至少兩度派出大軍討伐；到六一七年大業十三年，劉元進仍在歙州一帶活動，與舒州陳佛智、吳郡沈興國、杭州汪文進等同時並起。六一八年之後，隋的軍府體系崩解，這些起義軍或降唐、或散為盜、或被地方豪強收編，劉元進本人的結局在現存史籍中記載不一。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The rising is placed in the ninth year of Daye, that is 613 CE; both the Yandi ji of the Book of Sui and the Comprehensive Mirror give the month but no day, and it is generally put in the tenth or eleventh month of that year. Liu Yuanjin's rising was not an isolated outbreak: in the same year Liu Ziyuan rose in Wujun and proclaimed himself King of Wu, Yang Xuanggan moved in Liyang, and in Shandong the righteous army headed by Wang Bo had been up since earlier, while in the north Dou Jiande was enlarging his position in the parts of the empire the court could no longer hold. The Sui's own strength is likewise on record: the Comprehensive Mirror states that in the second campaign against Goguryeo in the Daye era the army numbered more than a million men; on the canal works, the Tongji Canal opened in the first year of Daye reached Jiangdu and the Yongji Canal opened in the fourth reached north to Zhuojun; and the Book of Sui, in the treatise on food and revenue, gives for the Daye era more than 8.9 million households and some 46 million mouths, so that the number of taxable persons and the volume of transport behind every soldier in the field were on a scale that suppression of this revolt could not easily bear. No reliable figure survives for the size of the rising itself: the histories give only round expressions of the kind 'tens of thousands', and the exact strength of Liu Yuanjin's force cannot be settled by anyone. What can be said is that he was not a small band of bandits but one of the forces the Sui court treated as the gravest threat in the Jianghuai. In time, from the rising in the winter of 613 to the fall of the Sui in 618 is at least four years, and the court sent out major armies against him at least twice. By 617, the thirteenth year of Daye, Liu Yuanjin was still active around Shezhou, rising together with Chen Fozhi in Shuzhou, Shen Xingguo in Wujun and Wang Wenjin in Hangzhou. After 618 the Sui's army prefectures fell apart, and these rebel bands either surrendered to the Tang, scattered into banditry, or were taken over by local magnates; the fate of Liu Yuanjin himself is given differently in the surviving histories.
cause: 起事的原因有三層。第一層是徭役與兵役：大業六年以後連續征高句麗，大業七年起煬帝兩度巡江都、又遊北塞，每次隨駕與漕轉的規模都在數十萬人，江淮正是承擔全部勞役與稅負的地區；大業元年開的通濟渠與大業四年開的永濟渠，把江南的米與人力沿河一線抽往北方。第二層是饑荒：江淮、江南一連數年歉收，糧價騰貴，豪門囤積閉糶，《資治通鑑》所記江都一帶已有人相食的慘況，農民被迫離田，逃入山林與江澤，剩下的一半成了盜寇。第三層是秩序本身的崩壞：府兵制一旦失效，郡縣官軍既無訓練也無裝備，鄉里不再有可信的秩序，而隋廷把能打的兵與精銳的騎兵都壓在遼東，江南只剩空架子。劉元進這樣的地方人物正是在這樣的縫隙裏聚眾：他要的不是改朝換代，而是趁官府真空，能守住徽州的山與水，就有立腳之地。同一時期吳郡劉子元、黎陽楊玄感先後起事，也說明大業九年的隋朝，已經沒有餘力同時壓住每一處。
causeEn: The outbreak had three layers of cause. The first was corvée and military service: after the sixth year of Daye came the repeated campaigns against Goguryeo, and from the seventh year Yangdi twice toured Jiangdu and travelled through the northern frontier, each time taking tens of thousands with him and setting up an enormous train of transport, and the Jianghuai was precisely the region that carried the whole burden of the labour and the taxation. The Tongji Canal opened in the first year of Daye and the Yongji Canal opened in the fourth drew the rice and the labour of the south northwards along the water in a single line. The second was famine: for several successive years the harvest failed across the Jianghuai and the south, the price of grain soared, the great houses cornered the crop and closed their granaries, and the Comprehensive Mirror records conditions in the Jiangdu region in which people were eating one another; peasants were driven from the fields into the hills and the marshes, and half of those who stayed became bandits. The third was the breakdown of order itself. Once the fubing system failed, the county troops had neither training nor equipment, the countryside no longer had any order one could rely upon, and the court had concentrated every soldier who could fight and every body of cavalry in Liaodong, leaving only an empty shell in the south. A local figure such as Liu Yuanjin gathered his following in exactly such a gap: what he wanted was not a change of dynasty but a share of the vacuum left by the absent authorities, and if he could hold the mountains and the water of Huizhou he would have somewhere to stand. That Liu Ziyuan in Wujun and Yang Xuanggan at Liyang also rose in the same year shows that in the ninth year of Daye the Sui no longer had the strength to hold down every outbreak at once.
impact: 這場叛亂對隋朝的傷害不在戰場，而在它撕開了江南防務的破口。為平徽州，隋廷不得不從江都、丹陽抽調宿衛與募兵，又不敢從遼東前線多抽人，結果是前線與後方同時變薄；六一三年之內吳郡劉子元、黎陽楊玄感、歙州劉元進三處並發，隋朝首尾不能相顧，徵兵、轉輸、糧價與民心互相拖累，最終演成六一八年的改朝換代。對江南社會而言，戰亂與隨後的鎮壓破壞了徽州與鄰近地區的編戶與里坊秩序，流民四散，豪強趁勢兼併土地，隋亡之後江南成為各方接續爭奪的舞台：沈興國、汪文進、陳佛智等一個接一個起兵，直到唐室才逐一削平，這套收拾江南的經驗也成為唐初州縣與羈縻並用的政策的來歷。軍器層面，這場戰爭留下的是一個關於後勤的教訓：起義軍未必輸在戰鬥力，多數是輸在沒有攻城器械、沒有騎兵、沒有穩定的糧源；隋軍屢次平叛屢次不克，也是同樣的道理。
impactEn: The damage this revolt did to the Sui was not done on the battlefield but in the breach it tore in the defences of the south. To put down Huizhou the court had to draw garrison troops and hired soldiers away from Jiangdu and Danyang, while it dared not take many more men off the Liaodong front; the result was that both the front and the rear grew thin at once. In the single year 613 there were outbreaks at Wujun under Liu Ziyuan, at Liyang under Yang Xuanggan and at Shezhou under Liu Yuanjin, and the Sui could not attend to more than one of them: conscription, transport, the price of grain and the mood of the people dragged on one another, until the whole thing came to the change of dynasty in 618. For the society of the south, the war and the repression that followed broke up the registers and the ward organisation of Huizhou and its neighbours, the displaced scattered, and the powerful houses took the opportunity to swallow land. After the fall of the Sui, Jiangnan became a stage on which one party after another contended: Shen Xingguo, Wang Wenjin and Chen Fozhi rose one after another, and only the Tang court put them down in turn, and the experience of settling the south that followed fed into the Tang policy of combining regular counties with indirect rule. On the side of arms and equipment, the war left a lesson about logistics: the insurgents were not necessarily defeated in the fighting, most often they were defeated by the lack of siege engines, of cavalry and of a steady supply of food, and the Sui army's failure to settle one rebellion after another was a matter of the same kind.
result: 劉元進起義的結局，與李密、竇建德那樣終於建國號、割據一方的人不同：它沒有走出徽州。隋廷視他為江淮心腹之患，先後遣軍討伐，數度將他打散，數度又讓他復起；到大業十三年他仍在歙州、黟縣一帶活動，並與舒州陳佛智、吳郡沈興國、杭州汪文進等遙相呼應，隋廷被迫分頭用兵，戰線拉長而力量分散，一處剛平一處又起。618年隋朝崩潰後，隋的軍府與府兵編制一併瓦解，起義軍或降於唐、或散為盜寇、或被地方豪強收編，劉元進本人的下落在現存史籍中說法不一，多數只能確定他沒有在江南建立任何政權，也沒有留下可考的結局。戰爭真正的終局，是由另一種力量來收的場：唐室在江南花了數年，先後平定沈興國、汪文進、陳佛智等殘部，才把徽州與吳越的秩序重新理順；對後人而言，613年這場在史料中只留下寥寥數行的起義，成為隋朝崩解的注腳，也成為隋末江南軍亂的一個樣本。
resultEn: The outcome of Liu Yuanjin's rising was unlike that of men such as Li Mi or Dou Jiande, who in the end raised a dynastic title and held a region of their own: it never got out of Huizhou. The court treated him as the bane of the Jianghuai and sent armies against him more than once, scattering him more than once and letting him rise again as many times. In the thirteenth year of Daye he was still active around Shezhou and Yi county, answering in concert with Chen Fozhi in Shuzhou, Shen Xingguo in Wujun and Wang Wenjin in Hangzhou, so that the court had to divide its forces, the line of operations lengthened and its strength was spread thin, one outbreak settled just as another began. When the Sui collapsed in 618 the army prefectures and the fubing structure fell apart with it, and the rebel bands either surrendered to the Tang, scattered into banditry, or were absorbed by local magnates. What the surviving histories say about Liu Yuanjin's own fate differs; all that can be held with certainty is that he established no regime in the south and left no traceable ending. The war was in truth closed by a different power: the Tang court spent several years in the south, putting down in turn the remnants of Shen Xingguo, Wang Wenjin and Chen Fozhi before the order of Huizhou and of the Wu-Yue region was set right again. For those who came after, this rising of 613, of which the records preserve only a few lines, stands as a footnote to the dissolution of the Sui and as a specimen of the military revolts that shook the south in the last years of the dynasty.
